name: Australian Convict Sites
description: Eleven former prison sites scattered from Fremantle in Western Australia to Norfolk Island, with clusters around Sydney and in Tasmania, preserve the story of Britain's convict transportation. Between 1787 and 1868, about 166,000 men, women and children were shipped here. Visitors can walk through the barracks, prisons and work settlements where convicts were punished, put to forced labour, and set to building the colonies.
